title: Supervisor Intent v1
description: One turn of the read-only supervisor in `ask` (research mode) or the material analyst (analysis mode): the model classifies free text as a CLI query, a grounded answer, a pending-approval Decision request, or unclear, and the CLI routes on exactly that value. What is checked: the payload is an object, `kind` is present, and the companion fields carry the types the routing code reads them as. What is deliberately NOT checked: the per-kind conditionals the prompt states in prose (answer optional on a query, cliArgs null unless querying, summary+reason on a pending-action) — a model that drops one still has to be routed, and ask.ts degrades every missing field safely (unknown kind → unclear, argv outside the read-only list → a pending Decision, never an executed change). Whether the answer is really grounded, and whether the classification is right, is judgement that stays with the agent and src/commands/ask.ts.

kind.description: The prompt offers query | answer | pending-action | unclear, but no enum is set: ask.ts treats any unrecognised value as unclear rather than failing the turn, and an enum here would turn that graceful degrade into an aborted run.

answer.description: The evidence-grounded reply shown to the user, or the one-line summary of a query.

cliArgs.description: argv for the read-only CLI to relay (e.g. ["status"]). Never trusted as sent: only kind=query uses it and the platform re-sanitizes it against the read-only command list.

reason.description: Which high-impact area a pending-action touches. Plain string, not the prompt's six labels: the value is only ever written into the Decision text, and the deterministic fake harness reports its own label.

summary.description: The request restated for the audit log.
